opening_actions: The captain looks from a packed fish rack, coconuts, and full water barrel down to a plate holding only fish and coconut.
He pauses and raises one eyebrow at the mismatch between abundance and repetition.
He lifts the spyglass correctly to his visible unpatched eye and studies the repeated foods.

entry_bridge.a_end: The captain holds the spyglass toward the fish, coconuts, and narrow meal, with the small eyepiece beside his visible unpatched eye and the wider objective facing the food.
entry_bridge.b_start: At the editorial seam, an oblique rear-side view clearly shows the same correct spyglass orientation, supporting grip, subject direction, and island-shelter lighting before matching into his outward-looking viewpoint.
entry_bridge.reveal: The forward view shifts from apparent food abundance to a closer comparison of what the repeated meals provide and what a very narrow diet can miss.
entry_bridge.world_entry: The spyglass framing disappears into a full-bleed, host-free comparison of repeated island meals against the broader mix of nutrients a human body needs over time.

episode_direction.opening_activity: testing whether abundant food also provides enough dietary variety for long-term survival
episode_direction.opening_location: a simple island food shelter beside coconut trees
episode_direction.opening_environment: A shaded open-sided food shelter on an uninhabited tropical island, stocked with drying fish, gathered coconuts, a full clean-water barrel, and a small meal-preparation surface.
episode_direction.topic_visual_link: The island visibly has plenty of food and water, yet the captain's meal repeats the same two foods, directly exposing the difference between having enough to eat and having a sufficiently varied long-term diet.
episode_direction.opening_visual_proof: A visibly abundant rack of fish, pile of coconuts, and full water barrel surround a meal plate containing only fish and coconut.
episode_direction.curiosity_trigger: The captain notices that despite food filling the shelter, his plate looks almost identical to the meals available around it.
episode_direction.trigger_object: the narrow fish-and-coconut meal sitting amid abundant supplies of the same foods
episode_direction.reaction: He gives the plate a brief skeptical look, raises one eyebrow, and pauses before investigating further.
episode_direction.entry_retrieval: After comparing the full stores with the repetitive plate, he reaches for the resting spyglass and angles it toward the foods to inspect the pattern more closely.
episode_direction.world_style_hint: A bright, grounded tropical survival world that transitions into clear host-free visual comparisons of meals, nutrients, water, shelter, medical risk, and aging.
episode_direction.reason: The abundance-versus-variety mismatch makes the script's opening nutrition question visible immediately and gives the seasoned explorer a natural discrepancy to investigate without changing the selected island premise.

body: Health also needs vitamins, minerals, protein, and fats.
Eating only a few foods may still leave nutrient gaps.
Over time, those gaps can cause health problems.
Fresh plants may add nutrients those repeated meals miss.
Clean drinking water is essential every day.
Shelter protects you from heat, rain, and storms.
Injuries or infections can become dangerous without medical care.
Even perfect nutrition cannot stop normal aging.
script_plan.optional_closing: Plenty of food helps, but it cannot make you live forever.
